messages.author: 55d0e2f87b0f795e
messages.subject: speed with vectorization?
parts:
Hi TMB users,

This is a very basic question, so I’m sorry if it’s been covered somewhere already. I couldn’t find the answer elsewhere.

Is there any speed improvement from replacing for-loops with vectorized operations? My first guess is that the answer is "no", based on the fact that the code to vectorize all the functions is written with for-loops (https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/master/TMB/inst/include/Vectorize.hpp), but there might be a complexity of compiling that I’m not aware of.

cheers,
Mollie

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: speed with vectorization?
parts: You are right: TMB vectorization doesn't offer speedups over for-loops. In fact, a manual for-loop may in theory be faster if you squeeze a lot of work into the body of the loop...

messages.author: 4453e5ef4c1cb06e
messages.subject: Re: speed with vectorization?
parts:
My understanding of the Stan package is they get speedups from vectorization from their likelihood calculations b/c they can smartly calculate the constants (see https://mc-stan.org/docs/2_26/stan-users-guide/vectorization.html#vectorized-probability-functions).

I wonder if something similar would work with TMB, and be worth doing?

Hmmm. Is there a nice clean implementation of memoization that would
work with TMB? e.g. this would make a good way to avoid recomputing
normalization constants - although I don't know how much these
computations actually cost relative to everything else. (These
constants can typically be completely omitted from log-likelihood
calculations, but there are times when it is way more convenient to have
the complete log-likelihoods - so - *if* this actually has a
computational impact - it would be convenient to ignore them during the
optimization phase ...

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: speed with vectorization?
parts:
OK, I should have been a bit more specific on the vectorization comments:

Vectorization only affects a very tiny portion (say 1 percent) of a TMB model, i.e. the part that builds the computational graph.
Sure, you could make this part run faster but you would hardly notice a difference in overall runtime.

This is in contrast to Stan that builds the graph on each function evaluation. Here vectorization matters a lot.

Memorization is already being used by the current release of TMB, but future TMB versions will take even more advantage of memorization (caching of temporaries). If you are interested in the effect it has on glmmTMB try installing TMB from the branch 'TMB_experimental'.
